/-!
# Erdős Problem 63

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/63](https://www.erdosproblems.com/63)
- [dBEr51] de Bruijn, N. G. and Erdős, P., *A colour problem for infinite graphs and a problem
  in the theory of relations*. Indag. Math. (1951), 369--373.
- [ErHa66] Erdős, P. and Hajnal, A., *On chromatic number of graphs and set-systems*.
  Acta Math. Acad. Sci. Hungar. (1966), 61-99.
- [LiMo20] Liu, Hong and Montgomery, Richard, *A solution to Erdős and Hajnal's odd cycle problem*.
  arXiv:2010.15802 (2020).
- [Re24] Reiher, C., *Graphs of large girth*. arXiv:2403.13571 (2024).
-/

namespace Erdos63

/--
Does every graph with infinite chromatic number contain a cycle of length $2^n$ for infinitely
many $n$?

Conjectured by Mihók and Erdős. Solved affirmatively following the work of Liu and Montgomery
[LiMo20].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_63 :
    answer(True) ↔
      ∀ {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V), G.chromaticNumber = ⊤ →
        ∀ N : ℕ, ∃ n ≥ N, 2 ^ n ∈ G.cycleLengths := by
  sorry

-- TODO: Add variants of the problem.

end Erdos63

findings.description: The module reference [dBEr51] lists pages 369–373 (line 25), but the cited article occupies pages 371–373. This is only a bibliographic typo; the mathematical statement is unaffected.
findings.source_evidence: The publisher's Crossref record for DOI 10.1016/S1385-7258(51)50053-7 gives "page": "371-373" (https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1016%2FS1385-7258%2851%2950053-7). The original three-page article at https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1951-01.pdf and bibliography item [2] of Erdős–Hajnal (1966) agree. The aggregate Rényi bibliography does repeat the incorrect 369–373 range.

reformulations.difference: The Lean statement expresses infinite chromatic number as `G.chromaticNumber = ⊤` in ℕ∞, and infinitely many exponents as `∀ N : ℕ, ∃ n ≥ N, 2 ^ n ∈ G.cycleLengths`.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The chromatic-number hypothesis is equivalent to `∀ k : ℕ, ¬ G.Colorable k`, so it includes exactly all graphs requiring infinitely many colours, without distinguishing their infinite chromatic cardinals. A subset of ℕ is infinite exactly when it is unbounded; thus the conclusion is equivalent to `{n : ℕ | 2 ^ n ∈ G.cycleLengths}.Infinite`. Both characterizations and their universally quantified combination were proved in the scratch file without using the problem theorem.
